meta.name: @shakthizen/what-is-it
meta.description: Live Project Memory, Task Tracker & Interactive Wiki for Vibe Coding
meta.architectureSummary: A CLI (bin/what-is-it.js) that scans a target repo and persists a compressed binary state (.what-is-it.bin) describing its features, tasks, wiki docs, and React-Flow user journeys. `init` builds a fast, honest file-path-based baseline; the agent-run `/wii-init` deep pass replaces it with a verified model (real rationale, real flows, real per-screen SVG mockups). A local Node HTTP server exposes that state to a React dashboard (Feature Spec Explorer, Wiki Docs, Visual Flow Graph) over a REST API + SSE, with same-origin enforcement and payload validation on every write. The same bundle also exports statically for GitHub Pages.

features.title: Core Storage & Schema Engine
features.description: Zlib-compressed binary persistence, schema-driven progress computation, and payload validation.

subFeatures.title: Compressed Binary Persistence
subFeatures.what: Reads/writes .what-is-it.bin with a magic header, zlib deflate/inflate, and atomic rename-on-write.
subFeatures.why: Zero-bloat, instant-load state file that survives git diffs cleanly.
subFeatures.how: Node zlib.deflateSync/inflateSync + tmp-file rename in saveProjectData/loadProjectData.

subFeatures.title: Schema-Driven Progress Computation
subFeatures.what: computeProgress() derives feature/overall completion from SubFeature.status when subFeatures exist, falling back to legacy Task.status only when they don't.
subFeatures.why: Progress must reflect verified capability state, not a flat todo-list count.
subFeatures.how: Weighted ratio of implemented sub-features per feature, aggregated for overallProgress.

subFeatures.title: Payload Validation Guard
subFeatures.what: validateProjectData() structurally checks incoming JSON (schemaVersion, meta, features[], wiki[], flows[]) before it's ever compressed and written to disk.
subFeatures.why: The CLI `import` and the server's POST /api/project used to accept arbitrary JSON with zero validation, risking silent state corruption.
subFeatures.how: Manual shape-check function exported from schema.ts, called from both the CLI import command and the HTTP write endpoint.

subFeatures.title: Atomic Multi-Process File Locking
subFeatures.what: Advisory file lock protocol with timeout, auto-retry, and stale-lock eviction.
subFeatures.why: Two agents/background tasks writing .what-is-it.bin at once can race past the atomic-rename step and drop one write.
subFeatures.how: File descriptor locking or a lockfile convention before the atomic rename in saveProjectData.

features.title: Codebase Scanner & Baseline Synthesis
features.description: The two-stage model: a fast, honest file-path scan now backs `init`, with a separate deep agent pass for real understanding.

subFeatures.title: Real File-Based Feature Inventory
subFeatures.what: synthesizeProjectData() builds features/wiki/flows purely from what scanProject() actually found (real routes/components/services/CLI/core files) instead of a fixed narrative.
subFeatures.why: The previous synthesizer was hardcoded to describe what-is-it's own architecture on every project regardless of what was scanned — this was the core 'inaccurate init' defect.
subFeatures.how: One Feature per non-empty discovered category, one SubFeature per file (capped, with an overflow marker), plus always-present Testing/Documentation coverage features that honestly report `missing` when nothing was found.

subFeatures.title: Two-Phase Init → Deep-Pass Model
subFeatures.what: `init` never fabricates gaps or rationale; `/wii-init` (agent-driven) is the only place real Why/How and `missingDetails` get written.
subFeatures.why: Keeps 'what actually exists' (verifiable from files) strictly separate from 'what's missing/broken' (a judgment call requiring code comprehension).
subFeatures.how: init's baseline sub-features carry neutral 'discovered, not yet verified' language; the /wii-init workflow instructs Phase 1 (verify real features/flows) before Phase 2 (flag gaps).

features.title: CLI Command Suite
features.description: init/status/task/feature/export/import/schema/install-skill commands and the default local-dashboard launcher.

subFeatures.title: Command Dispatcher
subFeatures.what: Commander.js-based suite: init, status, schema, install-skill, task add/done/list, feature add, export, import.
subFeatures.why: Single entry point for both humans and agents to drive project memory from a shell.
subFeatures.how: Commander option definitions with picocolors output.

subFeatures.title: Task ↔ SubFeature Linked Completion
subFeatures.what: Task now carries an optional subFeatureId; `task done <id>` flips both the task and its linked SubFeature to implemented.
subFeatures.why: Previously `task done` only mutated the legacy Task list, which computeProgress ignores once a feature has subFeatures — marking tasks done had no visible effect on progress at all.
subFeatures.how: scanner.ts sets subFeatureId when synthesizing tasks 1:1 from sub-features; index.ts's `task done` handler looks up and updates the linked sub-feature before saving.

subFeatures.title: Direct Sub-Feature Status CLI Command
subFeatures.what: A command like `feature subfeature done <id>` to flip a single SubFeature's status without a full JSON re-import.
subFeatures.why: Right now the only way to change a SubFeature's status outside the Task-linked path is a complete `import` of a new state file.
subFeatures.how: New `feature subfeature` subcommand touching `features[].subFeatures[].status` directly.

subFeatures.title: Interactive Feature & Milestone CLI Wizard
subFeatures.what: Terminal questionnaire for guiding developers through feature/gap definitions interactively.
subFeatures.why: Accelerates setup for developers who prefer prompts over hand-writing JSON.
subFeatures.how: Integrate @clack/prompts or enquirer.

features.title: Multi-Agent Skill & Slash Command Installer
features.description: Generates SKILL.md, per-IDE slash commands, and the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules onboarding block.

subFeatures.title: Cross-IDE Rule & Slash Command Generator
subFeatures.what: Writes .agents/skills/what-is-it/SKILL.md, .agent/workflows/*.md, .claude/commands/*.md, .cursor/rules/what-is-it.mdc, and idempotently updates AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules/.windsurfrules/.clinerules via a marker block.
subFeatures.why: So every AI agent/IDE picks up the same project-memory protocol automatically.
subFeatures.how: Template string generation with project-specific path injection; marker-delimited block replacement on re-install.

subFeatures.title: Two-Phase Deep-Analysis Instructions
subFeatures.what: The generated /wii-init workflow now explicitly sequences Phase 1 (verify real features/flows, generate mockupSvg per screen) before Phase 2 (flag missing/bugs/security), instead of one flat list.
subFeatures.why: Previously the instructions didn't distinguish 'what exists' from 'what's missing', so an agent could conflate real features with wishlist gaps.
subFeatures.how: Rewrote generateDynamicSkill() section 6 and the wii-init.md template in installSkills().

features.title: Local Web Server & Live Sync
features.description: Zero-dependency HTTP server serving the SPA, a small REST API, and Server-Sent Events for live updates.

subFeatures.title: Static Asset Server, REST API & SSE Broadcast
subFeatures.what: Serves the built SPA, GET/POST /api/project, POST /api/task/toggle, and a text/event-stream /api/events channel that broadcasts on every fs.watch change to .what-is-it.bin.
subFeatures.why: One `npx what-is-it` command needs to serve a live-updating dashboard with no extra infra.
subFeatures.how: Node http module, MIME lookup, fs.watch debounce, held SSE response set.

subFeatures.title: Same-Origin Enforcement on /api/*
subFeatures.what: Every /api/* request is checked against Origin/Referer; anything not matching this server's own localhost:<port> (or lacking the header entirely, e.g. curl/the CLI) gets a 403.
subFeatures.why: The server previously sent `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on every response including preflights, so any webpage open in the same browser — visited before or after the dashboard — could read GET /api/project and, worse, POST to it or to /api/task/toggle with zero authentication. That's a classic localhost CSRF/data-exfiltration hole.
subFeatures.how: isTrustedOrigin() parses the Origin/Referer URL and compares hostname+port; the wildcard CORS headers were removed entirely rather than scoped, since the SPA is same-origin with its own API.

subFeatures.title: Request Payload Schema Validation on Write Endpoints
subFeatures.what: POST /api/project now runs the body through validateProjectData() and rejects (400) anything that doesn't match before calling saveProjectData().
subFeatures.why: Previously any JSON body — valid or not — was compressed and written straight to .what-is-it.bin.
subFeatures.how: Reuses core/schema.ts's validateProjectData().

subFeatures.title: Automated Test Coverage for Server Security Behavior
subFeatures.what: No test file exercises the HTTP server directly — the origin check, payload validation, and SSE broadcast were only verified manually (curl + a live browser CSRF attempt) during this session, not committed as a regression test.
subFeatures.why: Without a test, a future refactor of server.ts could silently reintroduce the wildcard-CORS/unvalidated-write hole this session just closed.
subFeatures.how: Spin up startServer() on an ephemeral port in a test, hit it with node's http/fetch using forged Origin headers and malformed bodies, assert 403/400.

subFeatures.title: Client SSE Reconnect with Exponential Backoff
subFeatures.what: EventSource reconnect currently relies on the browser's default retry; no backoff or offline banner.
subFeatures.why: Prevents a stale 'Reconnecting' indicator or a thundering-herd reconnect when the CLI server restarts.
subFeatures.how: Wrap EventSource with a manual backoff timer in App.tsx.

features.title: Web Dashboard: Feature Spec Explorer
features.description: The default tab — feature/sub-feature cards with 4-W drawers, filters, and a per-feature task checklist.

subFeatures.title: Feature/Sub-Feature Cards with 4-W Detail & Filters
subFeatures.what: Search + category/status/role filters over expandable sub-feature cards showing What/Why/How/Where/When and a 'Missing & Planned Gaps' callout.
subFeatures.why: Gives humans a browsable view of architecture without reading raw JSON.
subFeatures.how: React state-filtered rendering over ProjectData.features.

subFeatures.title: Per-Feature Task Checklist Wired to Live Toggle
subFeatures.what: Each feature now renders its linked legacy Tasks as real checkboxes; checking one calls the App-level handleToggleTask, which was previously fully implemented but never passed down to this component — a completely dead code path.
subFeatures.why: There was no way to mark anything done from the dashboard UI at all; only the CLI's `task done` worked (and even that didn't move progress until the linked-sub-feature fix above).
subFeatures.how: Added an onToggleTask prop and a checkbox list per feature in ProgressDashboard.tsx; wired it in App.tsx.

subFeatures.title: Dark/Light Theme Switcher
subFeatures.what: Persistent theme toggle; UI is currently dark-only.
subFeatures.why: Accessibility/preference support.
subFeatures.how: Tailwind dark-class toggle + CSS variables.

features.title: Web Dashboard: Wiki Docs Viewer
features.description: Sectioned markdown documentation with scroll-spy bookmarks.

subFeatures.title: Markdown Rendering with Scroll-Spy Bookmarks
subFeatures.what: marked-based renderer with heading IDs, a left page index, and a right-rail table of contents that highlights on scroll.
subFeatures.why: Lets architecture docs be authored as plain markdown but browsed like a real docs site.
subFeatures.how: Custom marked.Renderer + IntersectionObserver-free scroll listener.

subFeatures.title: XSS-Sanitized HTML/Link/Image Rendering
subFeatures.what: The renderer now escapes raw inline/block HTML tokens and restricts link/image URLs to http/https/mailto before the result ever reaches dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
subFeatures.why: Wiki content is written by `import`/the HTTP API — untrusted by the time it reaches the browser. marked passes raw HTML through by default, so a malicious wiki page (or a CSRF'd import) could previously execute arbitrary script in the dashboard.
subFeatures.how: Overrode renderer.html/link/image with escaping + protocol allowlisting; verified against real <script>/onerror/javascript: payloads in a live browser during this session.

features.title: Web Dashboard: Visual Flow Graph
features.description: React Flow canvas with actor/frame nodes and an inspector drawer, now supporting agent-generated per-screen mockups.

subFeatures.title: React Flow Canvas with Actor/Frame Nodes & Inspector Drawer
subFeatures.what: Desktop/mobile/modal frame nodes and actor nodes, connected by edges, with role filtering and a click-to-inspect drawer showing UI guidelines/layout blueprint.
subFeatures.why: Visualizes discovered/verified user flows instead of a flat feature list.
subFeatures.how: @xyflow/react custom node types + Drawer.tsx.

subFeatures.title: Agent-Generated Per-Screen SVG Mockups
subFeatures.what: FlowNodeData.mockupSvg lets an agent supply a real, screen-specific inline SVG; frame node components render it (sanitized: scripts/event handlers/unsafe URLs stripped) instead of the generic wireframe template, which remains the fallback when mockupSvg is absent.
subFeatures.why: Previously every screen rendered the exact same fixed browser-chrome/phone-bezel template regardless of what the screen actually looked like — there was no way for an agent's deep analysis to produce a real visual.
subFeatures.how: Added mockupSvg to the schema, a DOMParser-based sanitizeSvgMarkup() (src/web/sanitizeSvg.ts), and a render branch in each of DesktopFrameNode/MobileFrameNode/ModalFrameNode.

subFeatures.title: Mobile Touch Gestures & Minimap Zoom-to-Fit Toggle
subFeatures.what: Pinch-zoom/swipe support and a minimap zoom-to-fit control for the canvas.
subFeatures.why: Usability on touch devices.
subFeatures.how: React Flow touch gesture config.

features.title: Static Export & GitHub Pages Mode
features.description: The same SPA bundle can run with no server at all, reading a pre-exported data.json.

subFeatures.title: Static data.json Export with LocalStorage Task Overrides
subFeatures.what: scripts/export-static.js snapshots the current binary state to docs/data.json; the SPA falls back to fetching it when /api/project 404s, and persists task toggles to localStorage instead of a server.
subFeatures.why: Powers the GitHub Pages live demo and lets any project's exported docs/ folder work with zero backend.
subFeatures.how: Static export script + fetch-fallback chain + applyLocalOverrides() in App.tsx.

subFeatures.title: Persistent Docs-Mode Navigation
subFeatures.what: Switching tabs (Wiki/Graph/Specs) in static/GitHub-Pages mode no longer bounces back to the marketing landing page.
subFeatures.why: isLandingMode was gated on `window.location.hash.startsWith('#docs')`, but every tab switch overwrote the hash to a plain tab name (`#wiki`, `#flows`) — so clicking any nav tab after the first immediately re-triggered the landing page. Found and reproduced live with real clicks during this session's testing.
subFeatures.how: Replaced the hash-derived check with a persistent `hasEnteredDocs` React state flag that, once set, survives subsequent tab-hash changes.

features.title: Verification & CI
features.description: Automated tests and GitHub Actions workflows.

subFeatures.title: Unit & Integration Test Suite
subFeatures.what: 11 tests across storage/scanner/caveman-formatter/skills-installer/binary-security concurrency.
subFeatures.why: Regression safety for the core persistence and synthesis logic.
subFeatures.how: Node's built-in test runner (node:test) via tsx.

subFeatures.title: GitHub Actions CI (Deploy & Publish)
subFeatures.what: deploy.yml and publish.yml workflows exist for GitHub Pages deploy and npm publish.
subFeatures.why: Automates release and demo-site updates.
subFeatures.how: Standard GitHub Actions workflows.

subFeatures.title: Headless Visual Regression Tests for the Flow Canvas
subFeatures.what: No automated screenshot/interaction tests for the React Flow canvas, drawer, or the new mockupSvg render path.
subFeatures.why: Prevents silent rendering regressions in the SVG frame/mockup logic across dependency upgrades.
subFeatures.how: Playwright + pixel-diff snapshots.

wiki.title: Architecture & System Overview
wiki.content:
## High-Level Layers

```text
+----------------------------------------------------------------+
|  CLI (src/cli/index.ts)                                        |
|  init / status / task / feature / export / import / schema     |
+---------------------------+--------------------------------------+
                            |
                            v
+----------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Core Engine (src/core/*)                                       |
|  scanner.ts (baseline synthesis) -> storage.ts (compress/validate/write .what-is-it.bin) |
+---------------------------+--------------------------------------+
                            |
                            v
+----------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Local Server (src/cli/server.ts)                                |
|  Static SPA + REST API (/api/project, /api/task/toggle) + SSE   |
+---------------------------+--------------------------------------+
                            |
                            v
+----------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Web Dashboard (src/web/*)                                       |
|  Feature Spec Explorer | Wiki Docs | Visual Flow Graph            |
+----------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Data Flow

1. `init` scans the target repo by file path only and writes an honest baseline to `.what-is-it.bin`.
2. An AI agent runs `/wii-init`, actually reads the code, and `import`s a verified replacement (real rationale, real flows, real per-screen `mockupSvg`).
3. `npx what-is-it` starts the local server, which serves the SPA and streams SSE updates whenever `.what-is-it.bin` changes (e.g. from `task done`).
4. For GitHub Pages / no-server use, `scripts/export-static.js` snapshots the same state to `data.json`, and the SPA falls back to fetching that file.

## Tech Stack

- **CLI**: Commander.js, picocolors, Node's zlib for binary compression.
- **Web**: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4, `@xyflow/react` for the flow canvas, `marked` for wiki markdown.
- **Build**: `tsup` for the CLI bundle, `vite build` for the SPA, both checked into `dist/`/`docs/` for npm packaging and GitHub Pages.

wiki.title: The Two-Phase Init Model
wiki.content:
## Why Two Phases

Earlier versions of `init` tried to do deep analysis without reading any code, and ended up hardcoding a feature narrative that described what-is-it's *own* architecture on every project it ran against. The fix was to split responsibilities cleanly: `init` only ever claims what a file-path scan can actually verify; real understanding is deferred to an agent that can read source.

## Phase 1 — `init` (baseline)

- Detects frameworks/project type from manifests.
- Buckets files into routes/components/services/cli/core/tests/docs by path pattern.
- Emits one Feature per non-empty bucket, one SubFeature per file, with neutral 'discovered, not yet verified' rationale.
- Never invents `missingDetails` or guesses actor roles/personas.

## Phase 2 — `/wii-init` (deep pass)

Run as a slash command in an AI agent's chat. Instructed (see `.claude/commands/wii-init.md`) to, in strict order:
1. Actually read the code and replace the baseline's generic sub-features with real Why/How rationale and real user flows — including a real inline SVG `mockupSvg` per screen instead of the generic wireframe template.
2. **Only then** flag genuinely missing features, bugs, and security issues as separate `status: "missing"` entries, kept out of the 'what exists' inventory built in step 1.
3. `import` the result, replacing the baseline.

wiki.title: Security Model
wiki.content:
## Local Server Hardening

`src/cli/server.ts` used to send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on every response and accepted unvalidated JSON on `POST /api/project` — a classic localhost CSRF hole: any webpage open in the same browser could read or overwrite the dashboard's state. Fixed by:
- Rejecting any `/api/*` request whose Origin/Referer doesn't match this server's own `localhost:<port>` (no CORS headers are sent at all now, so the browser itself also blocks cross-origin reads).
- Running every write body through `validateProjectData()` before it touches disk.

Both were verified live during the audit: a genuine cross-origin `fetch()` from a different port was blocked by the browser before it reached the server, and a forged-`Origin` `curl` request was rejected server-side with 403.

## Content Sanitization

Two render paths take untrusted, agent/import-supplied content straight into the DOM:
- **Wiki markdown** (`WikiView.tsx`): raw HTML tokens are now escaped and link/image URLs restricted to http/https/mailto before `marked`'s output reaches `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
- **Agent-generated SVG mockups** (`FlowNodeData.mockupSvg`): `sanitizeSvgMarkup()` strips `<script>`, event-handler attributes, and unsafe URLs via `DOMParser`/`XMLSerializer` before the frame node components render it.

Both were verified against real `<script>`/`onerror`/`javascript:` payloads in a live browser.

## Known Remaining Gaps

- No automated regression test exercises the server's origin check or payload validation directly (`sub-server-security-tests`) — only manually verified this session.
- No multi-process file lock on `.what-is-it.bin` writes (`sub-storage-lock`) — concurrent agent writes can still race.
